items.title: Laurena Diggs and Carrie Boote Interview, 1959-05-25
items.q: Because I know some of the leading, just like Ethel Waters. Ethel Waters, she worked in a street fair with a fellow named James Seymour.

ctx.x: I'm sort of jumping around today, but, uh, you say you had piano teachers? Did you have a voice teacher, too?

Me? No, no. Just, what little I tried was just something I, you know. Mm-hm. they used to have organ grinders, you know, going around the street and you put the nickel and the man would play your piece. Well, most children save their nickels, you know, and when he'd come around, they'd get out there and dance up a breeze right on the street, you know. And there are so many children and so many people here. Years ago, if you wanted a piano player, you didn't have to go look all around. You could look out and see…
